checks.claim: A gas flame burns blue when air is mixed into the gas before it burns; without enough air it burns yellow and makes soot.
checks.why: Repair and appliance sources: a yellow flame means the gas is not mixing with enough air (incomplete combustion), giving soot; a blue flame is complete combustion.

sources.title: Why You Should Never Ignore a Gas Cooktop Yellow Burner Flame
What Does Black Soot Coming From Gas Stove Burners Mean?

checks.claim: A flame failure device shuts off the gas if a burner's flame goes out.
checks.why: A thermocouple in the flame keeps the valve open; when the flame goes out it cools and the valve shuts (Electrolux, Miele support, cooker parts guides).

checks.claim: Most gas stoves light with an electric spark igniter that clicks.
checks.why: Turning the knob opens the valve and the igniter beside the burner clicks out sparks that light the gas (Sears, Maytag).
